1. Core Clinical Tension: A 47-year-old diabetic male presented with high fevers, left hypochondriac pain, significant weight loss, and inflammatory arthritis, in the setting of prior empiric treatment for presumed smear-negative tuberculosis. Contrast CT revealed a ruptured splenic abscess, triggering a wide differential including disseminated tuberculosis, brucellosis, and hematologic malignancy, before microbiological isolation of Burkholderia pseudomallei revealed chronic visceral melioidosis.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission clinical encounter ends following baseline blood investigations, chest radiography, and abdominal ultrasound/CT imaging showing the splenic abscess with capsular breach, immediately prior to percutaneous abscess aspiration and send-out infectious/rheumatologic serologies.
3. Differential Distinctions: Pulmonary and splenic tuberculosis was strongly suspected due to prior treated apical disease and chronic wasting, but excluded by negative sputum AFB, negative aspirate PCR for tuberculosis, and bone marrow biopsy. Brucellosis and enteric fever were excluded by negative serologies. Chronic melioidosis was definitively confirmed when splenic abscess aspirate grew oxidase-positive bipolar-staining Gram-negative rods forming characteristic wrinkled violet umbonate colonies on Ashdown's selective medium.
case_prompt:
A 47-year-old Indian man presented with high-grade fever and left-sided pleuritic chest pain of 3 weeks' duration, accompanied by anorexia and an intentional 6-kg weight loss over the preceding month. He had no cough, hemoptysis, jaundice, or bowel symptoms. He had a 5-year history of diabetes mellitus managed with insulin therapy, was a reformed smoker, and reported chronic alcohol use. Two years earlier, he had been evaluated for hemoptysis and treated with a 6-month antimycobacterial regimen for sputum-negative pulmonary disease based on apical fibrotic changes. He had also been managed for small joint arthritis for the past 3 months. He denied recent travel to Northern Australia or Southeast Asia, and reported no history of direct soil exposure or personal/familial malignancy.

On physical examination, his vitals were stable, and body mass index was 17.8 kg/m². Chest examination revealed fine crepitations and diminished breath sounds in the right upper zone. Abdominal examination demonstrated tenderness in the left hypochondrium and moderate hepatosplenomegaly. Digital rectal examination revealed no bleeding or masses.

Laboratory evaluation revealed polymorphonuclear leukocytosis and an erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 70 mm/h. Fasting blood glucose was 236 mg/dL, postprandial glucose was 300 mg/dL, and urine glucose was 2%. Serum electrolytes, renal function, liver function tests, prothrombin time, amylase, and lipase were within normal limits. Viral serologies for HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C were non-reactive. Chest radiography demonstrated right upper zone fibrosis. Upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopies were normal. Transabdominal ultrasound showed a heterogeneous collection near the inferior pole of the spleen suggestive of perisplenic abscess. Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT demonstrated a splenic abscess with a breach in the capsule and extension into the perisplenic space.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered strongly due to the patient's prior history of treated sputum-negative pulmonary disease, apical fibrosis, chronic fevers, weight loss, and splenic lesion; ruled out by negative sputum acid-fast bacilli smears and negative tuberculosis PCR from the splenic abscess aspirate.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Two years ago, the patient was evaluated for hemoptysis, diagnosed as sputum-negative pulmonary TB on the basis of X-ray finding suggestive of right upper lobe fibrosis... His sputum was negative for acid-fast bacillus... Polymerase chain reaction for TB was negative in the aspirate.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered in light of persistent fevers, hepatosplenomegaly, splenic abscess, and peripheral small-joint arthritis; ruled out by negative brucella serological testing.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Infectious screen was negative for enteric fever, malaria and brucella serology.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Lymphoma or systemic connective tissue disease
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to B-symptoms (fever, weight loss), hepatosplenomegaly, high ESR, and positive rheumatoid factor; ruled out by normal trephine bone marrow biopsy, normal tumor markers, negative anti-CCP, and absent antinuclear antibodies.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: He had positive rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated protein was negative. Anti-nuclear antibodies were absent and tumor markers were WNL. Trephine biopsy of the bone marrow was normal.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Percutaneous aspirate from the splenic abscess revealed catalase- and oxidase-positive, bipolar-staining Gram-negative bacilli that grew characteristic violet colonies with central umbonation on Ashdown's selective agar, confirming Burkholderia pseudomallei infection with subsequent complete cure on ceftazidime and co-trimoxazole.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The aspirate from the abscess revealed catalase- and oxidase-positive, gram-negative bacillus with bipolar staining and violet colonies with central umbonation in Ashdown's selective agar (Fig. 2), diagnostic of Burkholderia pseudomallei.

editor_comments: Chronic melioidosis frequently mimics tuberculosis, particularly in diabetic patients from endemic regions presenting with upper-lobe fibrocavitary changes and visceral abscesses. Culturing aspirated pus on Ashdown's selective medium is critical for establishing the diagnosis.
